comment: External AI models and weights, and whether this repo's permissive-only posture (THESIS.md 35) permits them. Not npm dependencies -- scripts/license-audit.mjs walks the npm production tree and cannot see any of this. Verdicts are recorded here so a restricted model is named as blocked rather than discovered at ship time. See docs/EXTERNAL-MODEL-LICENCES.md for the cited text behind every verdict.

verdicts.ALLOWED: Permissive terms. Usable on the same footing as an npm dependency.
verdicts.ALLOWED_WITH_CONDITIONS: Commercial use is granted, but the grant carries obligations or is revocable. Conditions are listed and must be honoured at the point of use.
verdicts.BLOCKED: Terms forbid commercial or production use, or grant nothing. Must not be designed into a feature.

staleness.comment: A recorded verdict is a measurement with a shelf life. The NVIDIA Open Model grant is revocable and incorporates acceptable-use terms by reference, so it can change without this file moving. Past warnAfterDays the audit warns; past failAfterDays it fails. A per-model checkedAt overrides the manifest-wide one, so re-checking one model does not claim the others were re-checked.

models.name: Kimodo (inference code)
models.reason: GitHub-detected SPDX Apache-2.0; on the audit's existing permissive allowlist.

models.name: Kimodo-SOMA-RP-v1.1, Kimodo-SOMA-SEED-v1.1, Kimodo-SOMA-RP-v1, Kimodo-G1-RP-v1, Kimodo-SOMA-SEED-v1, Kimodo-G1-SEED-v1
models.reason: The licence states models are commercially usable and grants sell/offer-for-sale/distribute rights. But the grant is revocable, which MIT and Apache-2.0 are not, so it is not equivalent to a permissive licence and is recorded separately.
conditions: Ship a NOTICE file reading 'Licensed by NVIDIA Corporation under the NVIDIA Open Model License' and pass a copy of the agreement to recipients (section 3.1).
Use must stay consistent with NVIDIA's Trustworthy AI terms, incorporated by reference (section 2.3).
Rights terminate automatically on bypassing or weakening any safety guardrail (section 2.1), and on instituting copyright or patent litigation against NVIDIA (section 2.1).
The grant is revocable (section 2.2). Treat availability as a dependency that can be withdrawn.
models.attribution: Licensed by NVIDIA Corporation under the NVIDIA Open Model License

models.name: Kimodo-SMPLX-RP-v1
models.licence: NVIDIA Internal Scientific Research and Development Model License
models.reason: Section 3.1 forbids distribution, deployment and production use outright, and forbids using the model to generate works for sale or distribution. That is exactly what this product does. The other six Kimodo checkpoints are NOT blocked -- the licence varies per checkpoint within one release.

models.name: PartField (code and weights)
models.role: candidate for element-level perception, phase A6
models.reason: Section 3.3 is an explicit use limitation: the work and any derivative works may be used only non-commercially, defined as non-commercial research and education. This restricts USE, not merely distribution, so serving it over HTTP does not escape it. Separately, the published checkpoint is hosted on a personal account with no declared licence at all, which grants nothing.

models.name: SAMPart3D (code and weights)
models.role: candidate for element-level perception, phase A6
models.reason: MIT on both halves: GitHub-detected SPDX MIT on the repository, and the Hugging Face model card declares mit, ungated. The unblocked alternative to PartField for A6.

models.name: UniRig (code and weights)
models.role: candidate for auto-rigging, unscheduled and gated on the geometry track
models.reason: MIT on both halves: GitHub-detected SPDX MIT on the repository, and the Hugging Face model card declares mit, ungated. Licensing is not what gates this one -- point-data survival on the geometry track is.

models.name: TRELLIS (inference code)
models.reason: MIT, copyright Microsoft Corporation. But the README grants MIT to 'TRELLIS models and the MAJORITY of the code' -- that hedge is load-bearing. Two submodules are excluded and carry their own terms: diffoctreerast (derived from diff-gaussian-rasterization) and a modified Flexicubes. Both are recorded separately. This verdict covers the MIT portion only.

models.name: TRELLIS-image-large and siblings (weights)
models.role: candidate for text-to-3D weights, phase A4
models.reason: The model card declares MIT, and the README says the models are MIT alongside the code. The WEIGHTS are genuinely unencumbered. This is true and, on its own, misleading: what turns TRELLIS's output into a mesh is the reference pipeline, not the weights, and that pipeline is blocked below.

models.name: InstantMesh (inference code)
models.role: candidate for text-to-3D / image-to-3D, phase A4
models.reason: Apache-2.0, on the audit's existing permissive allowlist. The code proper is clean; its declared dependency set is not -- see nvdiffrast.

models.name: InstantMesh (weights)
models.role: candidate for text-to-3D / image-to-3D weights, phase A4
models.reason: The model card declares apache-2.0. Same shape as TRELLIS: the weights are clean and the mesh-extraction dependency is not.

models.name: nvdiffrast (NVlabs)
models.role: mesh-extraction dependency of BOTH text-to-3D candidates, phase A4 -- the deciding entry
models.reason: Section 3.3 restricts USE, not distribution: 'The Work and any derivative works thereof only may be used or intended for use non-commercially... non-commercially means for research or evaluation purposes only and not for any direct or indirect monetary gain.' That is verbatim the clause PartField is already blocked under, so the ComfyUI over-HTTP carve-out does not reach it either (finding 2 in EXTERNAL-MODEL-LICENCES.md). It matters here because it is not an optional extra: InstantMesh's requirements.txt installs it directly ('git+https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/') and TRELLIS's install instructions name it. Mesh extraction is precisely the stage phase A4 needs, so a permissive model reached through this pipeline is not permissively usable.

models.name: diff-gaussian-rasterization (Inria / MPII) -- the parent of TRELLIS's diffoctreerast
models.role: rendering dependency of TRELLIS, phase A4
models.reason: Non-commercial USE restriction: 'The Software may be used non-commercially, i.e., for research and/or evaluation purposes only' and 'THE USER CANNOT USE, EXPLOIT OR DISTRIBUTE THE SOFTWARE FOR COMMERCIAL PURPOSES WITHOUT PRIOR AND EXPLICIT CONSENT OF LICENSORS.' TRELLIS's diffoctreerast submodule is stated by its own README to derive from this project, so the restriction travels with the derivative. Commercial use requires contacting Inria.

models.name: Hunyuan3D 2.0 (Tencent)
models.role: candidate for text-to-3D, phase A4 -- rejected on terms
models.reason: Not an OSI-approved permissive licence, and it fails this repo's posture three separate ways. Territorial: 'THIS LICENSE AGREEMENT DOES NOT APPLY IN THE EUROPEAN UNION, UNITED KINGDOM AND SOUTH KOREA' -- there is no grant at all for users there. Scale: above 1 million monthly active users a separate licence must be requested from Tencent. Conduct: an Acceptable Use Policy is incorporated by reference. A licence that can stop applying based on where a user lives is not one a shipped feature can rest on.
